minetti_coeffs.source: Minetti et al. (2002) J Appl Physiol 93:1039-1046, energy cost of walking vs gradient i. Valid for -0.45 <= i <= 0.45; gradients outside are clamped to the range edge.

gradient_clamp.source: Validity range of the Minetti polynomial.

body_mass_kg.source: Team assumption, crew member nude mass.

suit_mass_kg.source: Team assumption for a planetary suit + life-support backpack. Order of magnitude of NASA exploration-suit studies; not a specific suit.

gravity_metabolic_factor.source: Team assumption. Reduced-gravity walking studies (e.g. Farley & McMahon 1992, J Appl Physiol 73:2709) show metabolic cost falls less than proportionally with gravity; we scale Earth cost by 0.55 at Mars 0.38 g. Approximation, not a fit.

suit_penalty.source: Team assumption, multiplier for pressurised-suit joint torque and gait changes. Exposed so judges can test sensitivity.

baseline_metabolic_w.source: Resting metabolic rate of an adult (~100 W), applied for every second of EVA.

science_stop_metabolic_w.source: Team assumption, light work (sampling, imaging) at a science stop.

science_stop_min.source: Team assumption, dwell time at each science target.

tobler_peak_kmh.source: Tobler (1993) hiking function, v = 6 exp(-3.5 |s + 0.05|) km/h, s = dh/dx.

suit_speed_factor.source: Team assumption. Apollo lunar EVA traverses were slower than Earth hiking speeds; scales Tobler to ~2.8 km/h on flat ground.

min_speed_ms.source: Floor to keep steep-but-passable cells finite.

max_slope_deg.source: Hard cutoff above which a cell is impassable. Team assumption for a suited crew member on loose regolith; configurable.

roughness_weight.source: Team assumption. Cost multiplier = 1 + roughness_weight * roughness_norm.

hazard_weight_safest.source: Team assumption. Extra multiplier on rock hazard used only by the "safest" objective.

roughness_window_m.source: Window for local std-dev of detrended elevation (roughness).

kj_per_litre_o2.source: Energy equivalent of oxygen at RQ ~0.82 (~4.8 kcal/L), standard physiology value.

initial_o2_kg.source: Team assumption, usable primary O2 for an 8 h class EVA suit.

reserve_frac.source: Team assumption, O2 that must remain on arrival at the habitat.

capacity_wh.source: Team assumption, suit battery usable energy.

suit_baseline_w.source: Team assumption, fans, pump, controller, displays.

heater_w.source: Team assumption, off by default; raised by cold-case scenarios.

reserve_frac.source: Team assumption, energy that must remain on arrival at the habitat.

max_duration_h.source: Planning horizon of the timeline and envelope animation.

envelope_timestep_s.source: Envelope frame interval (5 min), per the planning brief.

speed_mult.source: Team assumption, reduced visibility slows walking.

extra_power_w.source: Team assumption, extra heater/fan load in dust.

extra_reserve_frac.source: Team assumption, flight rule adds reserve under degraded conditions.

weights.source: Team assumption. Mars 2020 priorities (aqueous alteration, carbonates for biosignature preservation) weighted above primary igneous minerals.

candidate_count.source: Number of science hotspots offered to the orienteering solver.

habitat_antenna_m.source: Team assumption, height of a surface radio mast on the habitat. Direct line of sight only (no orbiter relay); terrain from the HiRISE DTM, Mars curvature included.

suit_antenna_m.source: Team assumption, suit radio antenna on the backpack / helmet of a standing crew member.

gcr_dose_equivalent_msv_per_day.source: Hassler et al. (2014) Science 343, 1244797: MSL RAD measured 0.64 +/- 0.12 mSv/day dose equivalent on the surface of Gale crater (absorbed dose 0.21 +/- 0.04 mGy/day). Used as the galactic-cosmic-ray baseline during an EVA; no suit shielding credited (conservative).

career_limit_msv.source: NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 1 Rev. B (2022) career effective dose limit of 600 mSv for all astronauts.

sep_shelter_warning_min.source: Team planning rule. Solar energetic particle onset can follow an alert by tens of minutes; the crew must be able to reach the habitat (shelter) within this time after an SEP alert, otherwise the route is flagged. Not a NASA flight rule.

speed_kmh.source: Apollo 15-17 Lunar Roving Vehicle traverse averages were roughly 7-10 km/h (max ~13 km/h); team assumption for an unpressurised Mars rover on the same terrain.

max_slope_deg.source: Team assumption, below the LRV design slope of 25 deg to keep margin on loose regolith.

crew_metabolic_w.source: Team assumption, seated driving in a pressurised suit (rest 100 W plus light work).

walkback_rule.source: Apollo LRV walkback constraint: a riding traverse is only allowed where the crew could walk home with their suit consumables if the rover failed. The return envelope for rover EVAs is therefore computed with walking costs.

feature_res_m.source: Resolution of the ML feature stack (2 m grid averaged 4 x 4); CRISM is 18 m, THEMIS 100 m.

n_units.source: Number of unsupervised terrain units (k-means). Fixed in advance, close to the number of USGS SIM 3464 units in the AOI, so the agreement score is not tuned to the reference map.

feature_weights.source: Team assumption. Similarity search weights composition and thermal (what the ground is made of) above shape (slope, roughness, relief).
